text: One joke on late-night TV emptied store shelves across America... for a shortage that didn't exist.
December 1973. Gas lines. Oil crisis. Everyone's already on edge.
A congressman warns the U.S. MAY face a toilet paper shortage... in a few months.
Johnny Carson tells about 20 million viewers: there's a toilet paper shortage.
Within days, carts are FULL of rolls.
Stores set limits. One raises the price from 39 to 69 cents a roll. Shelves are still empty.
But here's the thing... nobody was being dumb.
If you hear about a shortage, and the shelf is empty... buying extra is the SMART move.
Everyone made the smart move. And THAT was the shortage.
The factories never stopped. Carson later told viewers: there is no shortage.
A shortage doesn't need missing toilet paper. It just needs everyone to believe in it... at the same time.
